question.text:
The equivalent conductances of two strong electrolytes at infinite dilution in $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ (where ions move freely through a solution) at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ are given below:
$\wedge^{\circ} \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COONa}=91.0 \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~cm}^2$ /equiv
$\wedge_{\mathrm{HCl}}^{\circ}=426.2 \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~cm^2}$ / equiv
What additional information/quantity one needs to calculate $\wedge^{\circ}$ of an aqueous solution of acetic acid?

solution.text:
From Kohlrausch's law
$\Lambda_{\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}}^{\circ}=\Lambda_{\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COONa}}^{\circ}+\Lambda_{\mathrm{HCl}}^{\circ}-\Lambda_{\mathrm{NaCl}}^{\circ}$
Hence, (A) is the correct answer.
